rows.title: Discounted Pragmatic Cost

declaration_statements.fep003_pragmaticCost_succ:
theorem fep003_pragmaticCost_succ
    (discount : ENNReal) (stageCost : ℕ → ENNReal) (horizon : ℕ) :
    fep003_pragmaticCost discount stageCost (horizon + 1) =
      fep003_pragmaticCost discount stageCost horizon +
        discount ^ horizon * stageCost horizon
declaration_statements.fep003_pragmaticCost_zero:
theorem fep003_pragmaticCost_zero
    (discount : ENNReal) (stageCost : ℕ → ENNReal) :
    fep003_pragmaticCost discount stageCost 0 = 0
declaration_statements.fep003_pragmaticCost_mono:
theorem fep003_pragmaticCost_mono
    (discount : ENNReal) {cost₁ cost₂ : ℕ → ENNReal}
    (hcost : ∀ t, cost₁ t ≤ cost₂ t) (horizon : ℕ) :
    fep003_pragmaticCost discount cost₁ horizon ≤
      fep003_pragmaticCost discount cost₂ horizon
declaration_statements.fep003_pragmaticCost_horizon_succ:
theorem fep003_pragmaticCost_horizon_succ
    (discount : ENNReal) (stageCost : ℕ → ENNReal) (horizon : ℕ) :
    fep003_pragmaticCost discount stageCost horizon ≤
      fep003_pragmaticCost discount stageCost (horizon + 1)

maturity_record.invariant: Finite-horizon pragmatic cost is the discounted ENNReal sum of stage costs; horizon extension exposes the exact terminal increment, costs are pointwise monotone, and horizon extension is monotone.
maturity_record.assumption_review: All costs and the discount live in ENNReal, so nonnegativity and infinity are represented directly. This is the pragmatic-cost input to EFE; epistemic value and its sign are owned by fep-021.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: A positive stage cost at the newly exposed time adds the nonzero increment γ^T c_T; a zero horizon and pointwise-equal costs exercise the boundaries.

declaration_statements.fep033_bellman:
theorem fep033_bellman {State : Type*}
    (discount : ENNReal) (stageCost : State → ENNReal)
    (step : State → State) (terminalCost : State → ENNReal)
    (horizon : ℕ) (state : State) :
    fep033_value discount stageCost step terminalCost (horizon + 1) state =
      stageCost state + discount *
        fep033_value discount stageCost step terminalCost horizon (step state)
declaration_statements.fep033_value_mono:
theorem fep033_value_mono {State : Type*}
    (discount : ENNReal) {stage₁ stage₂ terminal₁ terminal₂ : State → ENNReal}
    (step : State → State) (hstage : ∀ state, stage₁ state ≤ stage₂ state)
    (hterminal : ∀ state, terminal₁ state ≤ terminal₂ state)
    (horizon : ℕ) (state : State) :
    fep033_value discount stage₁ step terminal₁ horizon state ≤
      fep033_value discount stage₂ step terminal₂ horizon state
declaration_statements.fep033_zeroDiscount:
theorem fep033_zeroDiscount {State : Type*}
    (stageCost : State → ENNReal) (step : State → State)
    (terminalCost : State → ENNReal) (horizon : ℕ) (state : State) :
    fep033_value 0 stageCost step terminalCost (horizon + 1) state =
      stageCost state

maturity_record.non_vacuity: A nonconstant transition and positive discount propagate later-state terminal and stage costs, while zero discount isolates the immediate cost exactly.

rows.title: Expected Information Gain via Measure KL

declaration_statements.fep041_expectedInformationGain_zero:
theorem fep041_expectedInformationGain_zero
    (predictive : Measure Obs)
    (posterior : Obs → Measure State)
    (prior : Measure State) [SigmaFinite prior]
    (hposterior : ∀ᵐ observation ∂predictive, posterior observation = prior) :
    fep041_expectedInformationGain predictive posterior prior = 0
declaration_statements.fep041_informationGain_nonneg:
theorem fep041_informationGain_nonneg (posterior prior : Measure State) :
    0 ≤ fep041_informationGain posterior prior
declaration_statements.fep041_informationGain_eq_zero_iff:
theorem fep041_informationGain_eq_zero_iff
    (posterior prior : Measure State)
    [IsFiniteMeasure posterior] [IsFiniteMeasure prior] :
    fep041_informationGain posterior prior = 0 ↔ posterior = prior

maturity_record.invariant: Information gain is native measure-valued KL divergence: it is nonnegative, separates finite posterior and prior measures, and its predictive expectation vanishes when observations leave the posterior unchanged almost everywhere.
maturity_record.assumption_review: KL separation requires finite measures. The zero expected-information theorem requires a sigma-finite prior and almost-everywhere posterior equality; it does not claim that every informative experiment has strictly positive expected gain.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: An observation-independent posterior equal to the prior yields zero gain, while any unequal finite posterior/prior pair has nonzero KL by separation.
maturity_record.acceptance_probe: native Lean compile of fep041_informationGain_nonneg, fep041_informationGain_eq_zero_iff, and fep041_expectedInformationGain_zero.

declaration_statements.fep047_forward_compose:
theorem fep047_forward_compose
    (outer inner : Factor) (incoming : State → ℝ) :
    fep047_forward outer (fep047_forward inner incoming) =
      fep047_forward (outer * inner) incoming
declaration_statements.fep047_forward_nonneg:
theorem fep047_forward_nonneg
    (factor : Factor) (incoming : State → ℝ)
    (hfactor : ∀ x y, 0 ≤ factor x y)
    (hincoming : ∀ y, 0 ≤ incoming y) (x : State) :
    0 ≤ fep047_forward factor incoming x
declaration_statements.fep047_forward_mono:
theorem fep047_forward_mono
    (factor : Factor) (incoming₁ incoming₂ : State → ℝ)
    (hfactor : ∀ x y, 0 ≤ factor x y)
    (hincoming : ∀ y, incoming₁ y ≤ incoming₂ y) (x : State) :
    fep047_forward factor incoming₁ x ≤
      fep047_forward factor incoming₂ x
declaration_statements.fep047_identity:
theorem fep047_identity (incoming : State → ℝ) :
    fep047_forward (1 : Factor) incoming = incoming

maturity_record.invariant: Finite sum-product forward propagation is matrix--vector multiplication: it preserves nonnegativity and order under nonnegative factors, has zero and identity laws, and composes exactly by matrix multiplication.
maturity_record.assumption_review: Nonnegativity and monotonicity require entrywise nonnegative factors and inputs. Identity and composition are unconditional algebraic laws. The row proves exact finite propagation, not normalization or loopy fixed-point convergence.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: Nonidentity dense matrices and nonconstant incoming vectors exercise genuine cross-state aggregation; two distinct factors exercise nontrivial composed propagation.

findings.exact_correction: For positive discount and positive new stage cost, the terminal increment is nonzero; strict growth of the total additionally requires the previous accumulated cost to be finite. Discount zero at positive horizons exposes the zero-increment boundary.

With positive inverse temperature and a two-policy support of unequal costs, lower cost receives a strictly larger positive weight. At inverse temperature zero the law is uniform on support; excluded policies have zero mass.

Posterior normalization holds in every fibre of the selected Markov version; Bayes reconstruction identifies the version only relative to the predictive observation law, so no unique pointwise Bayes ratio at null observations is asserted.

Nonnegativity preservation requires nonnegative factors and inputs. Order monotonicity requires nonnegative factors and pointwise ordered inputs, which may themselves be negative. Identity/composition are unconditional algebraic laws.
